OTIS.thesis_one_line: World's largest elevator/escalator maintenance business, whose annuity-like Service book is real, but two guidance cuts and a CEO retirement in 2026 argue for a starter position, not full weight.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance is cut a third time below the current $4.01-$4.05 range
Organic New Equipment sales stay negative for 4 or more consecutive quarters
Net debt / adjusted operating profit rises above 3.5x (from ~3.0x currently)
No permanent CEO successor is named by July 2027 (the outside date in the transition agreement)
Modernization order growth decelerates below 10% (constant currency) for two consecutive quarters (from +9% cc / backlog +24-26% cc in Q2 2026)
key_adverse_facts: Two consecutive FY2026 adjusted-EPS guidance cuts: initial guide implied ~mid-to-high-single-digit growth off FY2025's $4.05; cut to $4.20-$4.24 on 2026-04-22; cut again to $4.01-$4.05 (flat-to-down vs FY2025) on 2026-07-22
CEO Judy Marks (in role since the April-2020 spin) announced her retirement on 2026-09-15; successor search underway (Spencer Stuart retained), transition due by 2027-07-31 at the latest
Both segments' operating margin compressed YoY in Q2 2026: New Equipment 5.3%->3.1%, Service 24.9%->23.2%, despite 7% total revenue growth
Total shareholders' equity is negative (-$5.75bn at 30-Jun-2026), a legacy of spin-off accounting plus continued debt-funded buybacks/dividends
data_conflicts: Quant card trailing P/E (17.0x) does not cleanly reconcile with a TTM-GAAP-EPS-derived P/E of ~20.5x computed from XBRL data; likely an adjusted-EPS basis in the card, not resolved with certainty

Earnings-release qualitative framing of Service-margin strength sits alongside the primary segment table showing Service segment operating margin compressed 170bps YoY in Q2 2026 -- both are drawn from company sources, but the headline framing should not be taken at face value without checking the segment table
OTIS.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the Service annuity moat is real and well evidenced (67-70% of sales, 23%+ segment margin even after compression), but two guidance cuts plus a CEO transition in the same year make the next 2-3 quarters genuinely uncertain

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for OTIS (outside V1's ~92-name coverage), so there is nothing to reconcile; own reverse DCF implies ~2.9%/yr 10-year FCF growth at an 8.5% discount rate, below my ~4%/yr base case, i.e. the price is below (cheap relative to) my base case, but only modestly so given genuine execution risk.

OTIS.scenario_basis: Start FY26 adjusted EPS $4.03 (guide midpoint) vs $65.94 close (25-Sep-2026). Bear: 0%/yr EPS growth, exit P/E 12x, ~2.7% avg dividend yield. Base: 4%/yr EPS growth, exit P/E 16.4x (flat), ~2.6% avg dividend yield. Bull: 9%/yr EPS growth, exit P/E 19x, ~2.3% avg dividend yield.

PEP.thesis_one_line: Frito-Lay/Pepsi/Gatorade/Quaker global snacks-and-beverage leader, cheaper than Coca-Cola, but real core-EPS growth is only mid-single-digit and the GLP-1/health-shift headwind on snack volumes is unresolved.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters (from 2.4-2.6% in H1 2026)
FY2026 core EPS guidance (5-7% growth) is cut
Core operating margin falls below 16% for two consecutive quarters (from 16.8% in Q2 2026)
Net debt / EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ~2.3x currently)
The Baltimore public-nuisance case produces an adverse ruling with quantified damages
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026's 137% GAAP EPS growth is driven almost entirely by a $1,860m Q2-2025 intangible-asset impairment that did not recur, not by underlying improvement; core (non-GAAP) EPS grew only 4% in Q2 2026 and 6% year-to-date
Core operating margin compressed 40bps YoY in Q2 2026 (16.8% vs 17.2%), corroborating the triage's margin-compression flag

Baltimore, MD public-nuisance lawsuit against PepsiCo/Frito-Lay survives after most claims were dismissed with prejudice (21-Jul-2025); oral argument scheduled for the fiscal quarter ending 5-Sep-2026
Net debt of roughly $44.6bn against stockholders' equity of only $22.1bn (30-Jun-2026), funding both the dividend and a new $10bn buyback program
data_conflicts: Triage cited 'active activist-investor pressure (Elliott Management)' from general knowledge; a search of SEC EDGAR found no SC 13D or SC 13D/A filed against PepsiCo (CIK 77476) -- only routine passive SC 13G filings -- so this claim is unconfirmed by any primary ownership filing and should not be treated as an established activist campaign
PEP.confidence_in_thesis: medium - a defensive, cash-generative franchise with 54 consecutive years of dividend increases, but the GLP-1/health-shift headwind on core snacks volumes is a real structural question that two quarters of data cannot resolve either way

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for PEP (outside V1's ~92-name coverage), so there is nothing to reconcile; own reverse DCF implies ~3.5%/yr 10-year FCF growth at a 7.5% discount rate, below my ~5-6%/yr base case (matching FY2026 guidance's midpoint), i.e. the price is below (cheap relative to) my base case.

PEP.scenario_basis: Start FY26 core EPS ~$8.63 (guide midpoint, +6% off FY25's $8.14) vs $128.63 close (25-Sep-2026). Bear: 2%/yr core EPS growth, exit P/E 12x, ~4.2% avg dividend yield. Base: 6%/yr core EPS growth, exit P/E 14.9x (flat), ~3.9% avg dividend yield. Bull: 9%/yr core EPS growth, exit P/E 18x, ~3.3% avg dividend yield.

PPG.thesis_one_line: Global paints and coatings leader with six straight quarters of organic sales growth and guidance reaffirmed three times, at about 13.6x forward earnings; at a cost of equity consistent with a 5.17% Treasury the price roughly equals the evidence-based growth path, so conviction is halved.
kill_criteria: Consolidated organic sales growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the streak is currently 6 positive quarters)
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($7.70-$8.10) is cut
Net debt / EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ~2.2x currently)
Asbestos-related reserves increase by more than 2x the current $42m
Automotive OEM/refinish organic sales decline for 3 or more consecutive quarters
Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin down more than 100bp year on year (company outlook: flat to down 100bp), or an H2 2026 EPS run-rate below $3.64 (the low-end implied by the $7.70 guide).
key_adverse_facts: Organic growth, while positive for 6 straight quarters, is still low-single-digit and uneven: +1% Q1 2026, +4% Q2 2026, with organic growth in only 8 of 9 underlying businesses (automotive refinish/OEM softness)

Legacy asbestos-related reserves of $42m (30-Jun-2026) and an open (though financially immaterial) environmental/Clean Water Act matter tied to a former Ford City, PA glass-manufacturing waste-disposal site
Net debt of roughly $6.05bn against $8.59bn of equity (30-Jun-2026); moderate leverage (~2.2x net debt/EBITDA per the quant card)

Guidance midpoint needs H2 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.84 (+5.5%) after H1 growth of 3% ($4.06 vs $3.94); Q3 outlook has margin flat to -100bp, automotive refinish EBITDA margin was -300bp in Q2 and industrial coatings margin compression is expected in H2.
Cost of equity at a 5.17% Treasury is ~9.6% (beta 1.03-1.07); base-case 3-year return of 7.5% is below it.
data_conflicts: Triage cited 'activist and new-CEO pressure' as a re-rating catalyst; a search of SEC EDGAR found no SC 13D or SC 13D/A filed against PPG (CIK 79879) -- no activist stake could be confirmed via a primary ownership filing. Tim Knavish is confirmed as current Chairman/CEO from being quoted in the 2026 earnings releases, but the specific appointment date and any activist campaign were not independently verified against a primary filing in the time available
FY2026 adjusted EPS guide midpoint ($7.90) implies a forward P/E of ~13.6x versus the quant card's stated NTM P/E of 12.7x; not fully reconciled (possibly a different EPS basis or timing)

RA8: the dossier's 8.5% discount rate and 6-7% base were inconsistent with the 5.17% Treasury and a 4.2% guided EPS growth; FY2025 owner FCF is $1.11bn after SBC and TTM $1.37bn (H1 working-capital timing); Q3 report confirmed for 27 Oct 2026.
PPG.confidence_in_thesis: medium - six consecutive quarters of organic growth, guidance reaffirmed (never cut), falling net debt and no discretionary insider selling, but low-single-digit growth, an H2-weighted guide with margin pressure in the Q3 outlook, and no margin of safety at the corrected cost of equity

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: RA8 re-test (6 Oct 2026): owner FCF after SBC $1.25bn (FY2025 $1.11bn, TTM $1.37bn), market cap $23.97bn, CAPM cost of equity 9.6% (rf 5.17% + Blume beta 1.069 x ERP 4.14%; the dossier used 8.5%), terminal 3.0%. Implied 10-year FCF growth 5.75% (4.6% on TTM, 7.3% on FY2025 cash flow; 3.3% at the old 8.5%) against an evidence-based 5% base (guide +4.2% on $7.58, H1 +3%, organic +1% to +4%). In line; value at 5% growth $101.6 a share (-5.5%), at 6.5% $113.7 (+5.7%).

PPG.scenario_basis: Start FY26 adjusted EPS guide midpoint $7.90 vs $107.52 (25 Sep 2026). Bear: EPS +1%/yr, 11x, flat ~$2.90 dividend = exit $89.5 plus $8.70. Base: EPS +5%/yr (restated from 7%), 13.6x, dividend +4% = exit $124.4 plus $9.05. Bull: EPS +12%/yr, 16x, dividend +6% = exit $177.6 plus $9.23.
